Criteria text

Agent verification criteria, version 3

Revision from version1: replace its heuristic20mm forward wrist→palm offset with a fixed anatomical MCP-base alignment. The rotation, thresholds, stages, starts and pass rates are unchanged. Four public Wuji MCP bases are aligned with245 valid human-contact frames (980base vectors), using the existing measured-axis rotation. The median offset in MANO wrist coordinates is[0.00037287,−0.00806710,−0.00768845]m; mean base mismatch falls from21.44mm to4.65mm, with approximately4.1/1.3/2.5mm component scatter. This calculation uses anatomy and public geometry, not candidate actions or rollout poses. It supersedes the original heuristic for future suites; earlier gates retain criteria1. See research/sim_v2/validation/anatomical_calculation.json and reference_calibration.json.

These are my own simulation criteria for TASK.md, not an official evaluation. They are fixed before policy evaluation. Reference: reconstruction version 5, record r0012, research/recon_v12; native 436 frames at 30 Hz. The full 60-minute reconstruction stage ended at 2026-11-17T21:57:56Z.

Revision3 makes the previously implicit side-face retargeting explicit. Both demonstrations begin resting on +X. For each deployment object, compute its initial World-up direction in object coordinates; select the dominant signed X/Y resting normal, and fix S=Rz(kπ/2) with k=0(+X),1(+Y),2(−X),3(−Y). Apply this single S to the demonstrated palm-relative position and orientation for the entire object cycle. This preserves blade +Z and the demonstrated World wrist style when a charger starts on a different side; it does not turn a side-face change into an imposed90° wrist roll. The selection uses only the initial pose, never a fit to a candidate's motion. One demonstrated family (white or black) must meet every phase for that object; it cannot switch source families between phases. All35mm/35° thresholds,90% phase coverage, finger-turn requirements, starts, stages and pass rates remain unchanged. Earlier gates retain their original criteria. This correction is made before relying on ±Y-face controller rollouts. The source-face measurements and mapping are in research/sim_v2/reference_calibration.json.

Task interpretation and deployment coverage

A right Wuji Hand 1 on the Marvin arm must pick up 2 or 3 lying chargers, one at a time, turn each with its fingers while retaining an opposed grasp, carry it left, and release it standing independently with its blades up. The goal applies to every real object, including repeated kinds. Object order and handling order are free. Sliding the chargers left, turning them solely with the wrist, or passive pivoting in an unmoving grip does not perform the demonstrated skill.

Evaluation uses the full deployment start: centres x[.30,.46], y[-.42,-.24]m; arbitrary heading over the full circle; all four side-resting faces (±X,±Y, blade axis initially horizontal), both kinds in any mix, and object rows permuted between episodes. Half the episodes have 2 objects, half 3. Include touching and leaning configurations (at least25% touching; at least half of those leaning). Starts must be physically supported and settled; no restriction to the demonstration's reachable grasp heading. The reset arm and 1.5s ramp are simulated. Episodes last60s/1800policy steps unless a specified stop ends them.

Uncertain mass, centre of mass, inertia, friction/glove, grip(.25–1), joint delay/filter and table edges are varied within the documented simulation priors. The exact draws are frozen in the suite's start sampler. The policy sees exactly contract-v3 observations, including the default delayed/noisy/lost/flipped object-pose sensor; no true poses, contact, force, velocity or images. The evaluator may use true state to measure these criteria.

Evidence and interpretation of numbers

The white contact interval is frames73–211 (4.63s), black250–384 (4.50s). Visible finger-turn intervals are white110–143 (3.67–4.77s) and black309–326 (10.30–10.87s). In the refined reference, object rotation relative to the wrist in these intervals is about88° and74°, while the wrist itself turns about26° and18°. Contacting thumb/index/middle tip excursions in the wrist frame are roughly29–65mm. The plugs travel horizontally about.205/.212m. The modelled centre rises are about16/34mm; the depth of the visible carry is weakly observed and an explicit10±5mm unsupported-clearance prior is used. Initial/final support and exact upright pose are physical constraints, not independent sub-degree video measurements.

The final releases leave about7.5s and1.7s of stable standing. The reference's all10required quality checks pass, with full-vertex hand/plug penetration below1mm, no finger intersections, and opposed-contact fractions.983/.919. These are checks against the reconstruction and its own masks, not ground truth. Camera/scale uncertainty is correlated (~55mm absolute translation); relative contacts are much tighter. Event boundaries have approximately3–5frame uncertainty. See analysis/quantification.json, validation/report.json, NOTES.md, comparison video and viewer of r0012.

Ordered stages and exact episode checks

An episode must complete the following stages for each object in the order below. One object's lift→turn→carry→release cycle must finish before another object's lift begins. Incidental touches while separating a touching pair are permitted; simultaneous controlled carrying of two objects for≥.10s fails. The evaluator reports the ordered stages below and the first failed predicate. The gate also applies the named standard measurements.

1. grasp

The object rises at least.010m above its initial centre height and is held unsupported in thumb/opposing-finger contact for at least.30s. “Held” excludes fixed-environment and other-object support, as in d2s_measures; opposing contact must be on different sides of the housing (contact-point angle≥60° about its centre). This permits the support transition during acquisition.

Standard predicates, every object: max_rise_m >= .010, held_s >= .30, opposed_s >= .30. Ten millimetres is a conservative physical clearance criterion relative to the16/34mm reconstructed rises and approximately5mm relative-depth uncertainty;.30s spans9policy samples and several controller/filter response times, rejecting a transient touch.

2. reorient

Within one continuously opposed, unsupported grip, the object turns≥40° relative to the palm and≥60° in World. The accumulated relative rotation while finger joints are nearly still must be≤15°. Use the standard100ms window and.30rad/s joint-speed definition of passive rotation unchanged. In addition, both the contacting thumb and at least one opposing finger must move their contacting surface by≥6mm relative to the palm during the turn; movement of an unrelated finger does not satisfy this. The evaluator measures the contact links' kinematic motion in the palm frame, not the object's slipping contact point alone.

Standard predicates, every object: opposed_rel_rotation_deg >= 40, opposed_object_rotation_deg >= 60, passive_rel_rotation_deg <= 15, opposed_s >= .30. Forty degrees exceeds half the smaller measured74° turn (37°), allowing adaptation and reconstruction uncertainty without accepting wrist-only rotation. Six millimetres is well below the observed29mm minimum contacting-tip excursion, accommodating the different robot morphology while excluding a stationary grip. The15° passive allowance covers small slips and approximately10° orientation uncertainty; it is not a licence to obtain the reorientation by passive pivoting.

Wrist style is also checked in the true simulated palm pose. Choose and record one fixed human-wrist→Wuji-palm calibration from the model geometry before freezing the suite. Adapt the two demonstrated segments to each episode's own start/goal and, where needed, a documented opposite-side grasp for otherwise unreachable headings. This is a reference family for judging motion, never a runtime action script. Do not fit it to candidate rollouts. In each lift/turn/carry/placement phase, at least90% of samples must be within35° orientation and35mm object-relative position of the corresponding phase's retargeted reference family, allowing progress alignment within that phase rather than requiring the human timing. The orientation tolerance covers roughly10° reconstruction,5° anatomical-axis and15° IK/alternate-contact uncertainty, rounded conservatively. The position tolerance covers about a housing half-width plus15mm of contact relocation for the different hand. Record the fixed calibration, phase matching and any hardware reachability calculation with the simulation. If a threshold is infeasible, revise only with explicit hardware evidence and a new criteria record.

3. transport

The opposed/unsupported grasp carries the object from the right toward the goal, with at least.12m of positive-y displacement while held and no table-supported sliding used for that displacement. It reaches y≥−.10m. This.12m lower bound is below the minimum deployment displacement.14m and below the demonstrated.205/.212m moves, allowing separation and set-down motion. Total hand contact must last≥.50s, excluding a ballistic flick or instantaneous relocation.

Standard predicates, every object: hand_contact_s >= .50, final_y_m >= -.10. The evaluator additionally measures the held-only displacement, support transitions, sequential handling, and wrist style above. Dropping or tossing is not an alternative transport strategy; a recoverable drop does not end the episode automatically, but the required ordered held cycle must subsequently be completed.

4. placed

Throughout the last.50s, every object's body centre is inside x[.28,.48], y[-.10,.05]m, its +Z is within10° of World up, its centre is within.010m of its model's standing centre height on the table, and it touches the table and not the hand. Thus the initial right side is clear. All objects must remain placed until the episode ends; a later knock-over fails.

Use the task configuration's placement bounds. For the final stable interval require speed≤.010m/s and angular speed≤.10rad/s, the standard rest_at_end_s definition, which is a stricter stability margin than the configuration's.02m/s/.5rad/s. The demonstration leaves at least1.7s of apparent rest, so.50s is conservative and distinguishes a standing result from a momentary upright contact.

Eight standard predicates, every object: final_x_m >= .28, final_x_m <= .48, final_y_m >= -.10, final_y_m <= .05, final_axis_angle_deg <= 10 (object_axis[0,0,1],world_axis[0,0,1]), rest_at_end_s >= .50, touching_hand_at_end <= 0, touching_environment_at_end >= 1. Height and full final-window conditions are also checked directly by the evaluator.

Hardware, suite, pass rate and verdict

Every stage must pass, in order, with no hardware violation and no stop. Use the public arm controller/IK/response, finger limits/torque saturation/filter/delay, ramp and all canonical stops. A policy exception/timeout/invalid action is policy_failure. Time expiration at60s is not a stop. Do not ignore arm, parked-left-arm or table collisions. Record per-episode stops and measured results, including failures.

Freeze64distinct development starts and use128fresh final episodes, with the deployment distributions above and new sensor seeds. The suite's mastery/pass rate is at least.80, zero hardware-violation episodes, and the required final10ms p99 inference/replay timing. This is an agent-chosen empirical robustness target, not proof over all possible starts. Report Wilson intervals and stratify2/3objects, kinds, face/headings and touching/leaning starts. A task feasibility suite must use exactly the same evaluator/stages/predicates/start sampler and meet≥.25 with any honestly described controller before policy gates.

The final candidate must be one contract-v3 neural network trained from random weights with PPO, with no BC, teacher, scripted base controller, runtime planner or demonstration replay. Demonstration object/wrist poses shape the reward only. A final verdict names the iteration, criteria version and final gate, uses the gate's measured result, and states simulator approximations, uncertain object properties, observation loss and any untested deployment cases. There are no target rounds in this run.

The goal applies to every real object, including repeated kinds. Object order and handling order are free. Sliding the chargers left, turning them solely with the wrist, or passive pivoting in an unmoving grip does not perform the demonstrated skill.

Evaluation uses the full deployment start: centres x[.30,.46], y[-.42,-.24]m; arbitrary heading over the full circle; all four side-resting faces (±X,±Y, blade axis initially horizontal), both kinds in any mix, and object rows permuted between episodes. Half the episodes have 2 objects, half 3. Include touching and leaning configurations (at least25% touching; at least half of those leaning). Starts must be physically supported and settled; no restriction to the demonstration's reachable grasp heading. The reset arm and 1.5s ramp are simulated. Episodes last60s/1800policy steps unless a specified stop ends them.

Uncertain mass, centre of mass, inertia, friction/glove, grip(.25–1), joint delay/filter and table edges are varied within the documented simulation priors. The exact draws are frozen in the suite's start sampler. The policy sees exactly contract-v3 observations, including the default delayed/noisy/lost/flipped object-pose sensor; no true poses, contact, force, velocity or images. The evaluator may use true state to measure these criteria.

Evidence and interpretation of numbers

The white contact interval is frames73–211 (4.63s), black250–384 (4.50s). Visible finger-turn intervals are white110–143 (3.67–4.77s) and black309–326 (10.30–10.87s). In the refined reference, object rotation relative to the wrist in these intervals is about88° and74°, while the wrist itself turns about26° and18°. Contacting thumb/index/middle tip excursions in the wrist frame are roughly29–65mm. The plugs travel horizontally about.205/.212m. The modelled centre rises are about16/34mm; the depth of the visible carry is weakly observed and an explicit10±5mm unsupported-clearance prior is used. Initial/final support and exact upright pose are physical constraints, not independent sub-degree video measurements.

The final releases leave about7.5s and1.7s of stable standing. The reference's all10required quality checks pass, with full-vertex hand/plug penetration below1mm, no finger intersections, and opposed-contact fractions.983/.919. These are checks against the reconstruction and its own masks, not ground truth. Camera/scale uncertainty is correlated (~55mm absolute translation); relative contacts are much tighter. Event boundaries have approximately3–5frame uncertainty. See analysis/quantification.json, validation/report.json, NOTES.md, comparison video and viewer of r0012.

Ordered stages and exact episode checks

An episode must complete the following stages for each object in the order below. One object's lift→turn→carry→release cycle must finish before another object's lift begins. Incidental touches while separating a touching pair are permitted; simultaneous controlled carrying of two objects for≥.10s fails. The evaluator reports the ordered stages below and the first failed predicate. The gate also applies the named standard measurements.

1. grasp

The object rises at least.010m above its initial centre height and is held unsupported in thumb/opposing-finger contact for at least.30s. “Held” excludes fixed-environment and other-object support, as in d2s_measures; opposing contact must be on different sides of the housing (contact-point angle≥60° about its centre). This permits the support transition during acquisition.

Standard predicates, every object: max_rise_m >= .010, held_s >= .30, opposed_s >= .30. Ten millimetres is a conservative physical clearance criterion relative to the16/34mm reconstructed rises and approximately5mm relative-depth uncertainty;.30s spans9policy samples and several controller/filter response times, rejecting a transient touch.

2. reorient

Within one continuously opposed, unsupported grip, the object turns≥40° relative to the palm and≥60° in World. The accumulated relative rotation while finger joints are nearly still must be≤15°. Use the standard100ms window and.30rad/s joint-speed definition of passive rotation unchanged. In addition, both the contacting thumb and at least one opposing finger must move their contacting surface by≥6mm relative to the palm during the turn; movement of an unrelated finger does not satisfy this. The evaluator measures the contact links' kinematic motion in the palm frame, not the object's slipping contact point alone.

Standard predicates, every object: opposed_rel_rotation_deg >= 40, opposed_object_rotation_deg >= 60, passive_rel_rotation_deg <= 15, opposed_s >= .30. Forty degrees exceeds half the smaller measured74° turn (37°), allowing adaptation and reconstruction uncertainty without accepting wrist-only rotation. Six millimetres is well below the observed29mm minimum contacting-tip excursion, accommodating the different robot morphology while excluding a stationary grip. The15° passive allowance covers small slips and approximately10° orientation uncertainty; it is not a licence to obtain the reorientation by passive pivoting.

Wrist style is also checked in the true simulated palm pose. Choose and record one fixed human-wrist→Wuji-palm calibration from the model geometry before freezing the suite. Adapt the two demonstrated segments to each episode's own start/goal and, where needed, a documented opposite-side grasp for otherwise unreachable headings. This is a reference family for judging motion, never a runtime action script. Do not fit it to candidate rollouts. In each lift/turn/carry/placement phase, at least90% of samples must be within35° orientation and35mm object-relative position of the corresponding phase's retargeted reference family, allowing progress alignment within that phase rather than requiring the human timing. The orientation tolerance covers roughly10° reconstruction,5° anatomical-axis and15° IK/alternate-contact uncertainty, rounded conservatively. The position tolerance covers about a housing half-width plus15mm of contact relocation for the different hand. Record the fixed calibration, phase matching and any hardware reachability calculation with the simulation. If a threshold is infeasible, revise only with explicit hardware evidence and a new criteria record.

3. transport

The opposed/unsupported grasp carries the object from the right toward the goal, with at least.12m of positive-y displacement while held and no table-supported sliding used for that displacement. It reaches y≥−.10m. This.12m lower bound is below the minimum deployment displacement.14m and below the demonstrated.205/.212m moves, allowing separation and set-down motion. Total hand contact must last≥.50s, excluding a ballistic flick or instantaneous relocation.

Standard predicates, every object: hand_contact_s >= .50, final_y_m >= -.10. The evaluator additionally measures the held-only displacement, support transitions, sequential handling, and wrist style above. Dropping or tossing is not an alternative transport strategy; a recoverable drop does not end the episode automatically, but the required ordered held cycle must subsequently be completed.

4. placed

Throughout the last.50s, every object's body centre is inside x[.28,.48], y[-.10,.05]m, its +Z is within10° of World up, its centre is within.010m of its model's standing centre height on the table, and it touches the table and not the hand. Thus the initial right side is clear. All objects must remain placed until the episode ends; a later knock-over fails.

Use the task configuration's placement bounds. For the final stable interval require speed≤.010m/s and angular speed≤.10rad/s, the standard rest_at_end_s definition, which is a stricter stability margin than the configuration's.02m/s/.5rad/s. The demonstration leaves at least1.7s of apparent rest, so.50s is conservative and distinguishes a standing result from a momentary upright contact.

Eight standard predicates, every object: final_x_m >= .28, final_x_m <= .48, final_y_m >= -.10, final_y_m <= .05, final_axis_angle_deg <= 10 (object_axis[0,0,1],world_axis[0,0,1]), rest_at_end_s >= .50, touching_hand_at_end <= 0, touching_environment_at_end >= 1. Height and full final-window conditions are also checked directly by the evaluator.

Hardware, suite, pass rate and verdict

Every stage must pass, in order, with no hardware violation and no stop. Use the public arm controller/IK/response, finger limits/torque saturation/filter/delay, ramp and all canonical stops. A policy exception/timeout/invalid action is policy_failure. Time expiration at60s is not a stop. Do not ignore arm, parked-left-arm or table collisions. Record per-episode stops and measured results, including failures.

Freeze64distinct development starts and use128fresh final episodes, with the deployment distributions above and new sensor seeds. The suite's mastery/pass rate is at least.80, zero hardware-violation episodes, and the required final10ms p99 inference/replay timing. This is an agent-chosen empirical robustness target, not proof over all possible starts. Report Wilson intervals and stratify2/3objects, kinds, face/headings and touching/leaning starts. A task feasibility suite must use exactly the same evaluator/stages/predicates/start sampler and meet≥.25 with any honestly described controller before policy gates.

The final candidate must be one contract-v3 neural network trained from random weights with PPO, with no BC, teacher, scripted base controller, runtime planner or demonstration replay. Demonstration object/wrist poses shape the reward only. A final verdict names the iteration, criteria version and final gate, uses the gate's measured result, and states simulator approximations, uncertain object properties, observation loss and any untested deployment cases. There are no target rounds in this run.
